results.content:
NEW YORK, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- The U.S. Index of Consumer Sentiment slipped to 47.8 in September 2026, according to a preliminary reading released Friday by the University of Michigan (UM) Surveys of Consumers, down from the final reading of 51.7 in August 2026 and from the final reading of 55.1 in September 2025.

This is the second consecutive month consumer sentiment has receded.
results.title: U.S. consumer sentiment slips in September, inflation expectations rise

results.content:
September 12, 2026 – On Friday, the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Preliminary Results for September was released.  
  
Note: September 2024 Consumer Sentiment under President Biden was 70.1  
  
The following is from Surveys of Consumers Director Joanne Hsu: [...] Year-ahead inflation expectations jumped from 4.0% last month to 4.6% this month, the highest reading since June. The current reading substantially exceeds the 3.4% seen in February before the Iran conflict began, along with all 2024 readings. Long-run inflation expectations ticked up to 3.4%, ending three consecutive months at 3.3%. These expectations remain higher than their 2024 range of 2.8% to 3.2%.
